text: I really like this game. I find that it has a lot more depth then a game like Overwatch. The downside is that it does not have the number of players like OW, and matchmaking seems to be broken. I really do love the raids, but it's sad that getting a team of five people in a raid is quite rare. You are usually 2-3 manning it. When it does happen though, a five man raid is a lot of fun. Multiplayer is hit or miss. Everyone complains that there are 100's mixed with lower level players, but it really doesn't make a huge difference in my opinion. But, not being able to replenish a lost player due to connection error or a quit does hurt. Trying to hobble through to the end a person or two short is ususally met with the team voting to take the loss and end the match. When things go smooth, this game is an absolute blast. When you are still at the MM screen after 7 minutes, it really sucks. This game could use some love with regards to matchmaking, but otherwise it's pretty solid. I got it in the Humble Bundle, so I am extremely happy with my purchase. I could see people being butt hurt if they paid full price. If you like twitch shooters get OW, if you like depth, Battleborn is a pretty solid choice.

text: Thumbs up for this game. I play PvE only and a lot of people say this is a PvP Multiplayer game with some underwhelming PvE and solo-play elements. I personally disagree, but it depends on your playstyle I guess. I can only play 1-2h per day and usually I play 1-2 maps. I do not need a big story and the solo gameplay is fine for me. Always something that keeps me engaged to replay the maps...go for silver/gold, unlock heroes, grind some loot and experience, etc.. Some may find that shallow, I find it satisfying and engaging enough. Multiplayer PvE is great, no problems so far with random groups. Playing with friends is a blast of course! I only have a medicore system and game runs smooth on high settings. Pros: - Heroes offer a vast variety of playstyles: Sniper, Tank, Melee, Hybrid...you name it they have it - You need to adapt your playstyle for each hero - satisfiyng grind for loot, lvl-ups, rewrds, unlocks, ratings, etc. - easy to play and get into, but challenging on higher difficulty/hardcore - good gunplay and shooter mechanics - solo play und multiplayer PvE is fun to play (for me) Cons: - some escort missions can be stressful/tricky on the first attempts - 8 Maps only for PvE so far (more to come, but DLC policy) - pay for DLC´s Verdict: Is it worth the price? For me yes, because I get enough out of it (and thats solo and PvE only). But I can also see some flaws and it is far from perfect, but really great fun to play so far. If you are unsure wait for a discount, if you also like to play PvP then go for it, obviously most people think it shines even more on that side. I do despise the pay-for-DLC-policy, but I will wait to judge on that until they show up and then try to get them on a good discount.

text: I did not expect very much when I purchased this game.  This game was a pleasant surprise.   Although the genre is described as action, the requirements for success are sufficient to classify Battlestations Midway as action/strategy.   The ability to control virtually every ship and aircraft in each scenario provides a variety of means to achieve the objectives.   At the same time you can control all of the action and strategy with the use of the tactical map.  You have plenty of options.  In addition to the campaign, that  begins with Pearl Harbor and concludes with the last two scenarios at Midway, the ship challenge, plane challenge, and the submarine challenge will certainly test your skills as they are fairly difficult.  I highly recommend this game.

title: battlestations: midway
text: -- from piloting planes in air-to-air and air-to-ground combat, from single small PT boats to destroyers with artillery and anti-aircraft flak, to commanding entire fleets! Missions are varied well so you do a variety of tasks with both planes and ships.  Despite not doing the "Naval Academy" missions as I didn't know that was the tutorial missions in the game, I picked up on the controls and the way to play the game easy enough; though I do wish I had done the Tutorial as there's a ship repair screen I still don't really understand.  The game actually has a lot to do in it and is pretty well done! You can take command of individual pieces in the war (a specific plane, ship, etc) or more manage the war from the map and just tell the pieces where to go.  It's fabulous what you can do. + Great missions with a good variety of goals + You can take control of many individual pieces:  planes (in air-to-air, air-to-ground, and air-to-ship combat), and ships (using AA guns, torpedos, depth charges, and artillery) + You can manage the entire fleet from the map and let the computer control the individual pieces + The game offers 3 skill levels for the missions and the "Regular" offered a good challenge.  I had to redo several missions a number of times. + It's a good length of a game.  My campaign lasted 10 hours (and that's not counting the various training missions, or the other 11 challenge missions) + The graphics.  Even factoring in the release date of the game, I think the game (gameplay) looks pretty good; better than I was expecting given its age.  The videos, granted, are terrible on a variety of levels. + Has multiplayer, but hadn't tried it at all, but it's nice they put MP in the game. ~ Story.  The settings and missions themselves were great, but the videos between the missions where they tell the story of your character; that was borderline at best. ~ Some missions are a little long, and being new at the game and a good challenge, if you loose, that was almost an hour you have to redo.  (Ahem, a couple more times in my case cuz I didn't want to go down to Easy!) ~ I had to change the controls from the defaults on a few different pieces (eg: planes controls seem to be inverted for mouse anyway); but the game does allow you to change them to whatever. ~ Planes don't seem all that manouverable when flying manually.  It was a challenge for me just to fly the plane and even SEE the enemy at times.  :-D ~ Some control screens just aren't intuitive such as the ship repair screen.  Granted there's a tutorial, but it's a single screen; you'd think I could figure it out, but ... I'm not really sure what effect my changes are having. ~ The UI isn't the most intuitive either.  Again, it may have been covered in the tutorial, but the red/green circles by the targeting crosshairs; that took a bit to figure out.  (Number of circles = how many turrets/torpedos you have.  Red Circle = a particular turret/torpedo can't fire in the direction aiming, Green Circle means the turret/torpedo is ready to fire.  Red Flashing Circle means that turret/torpedo is reloading.) - The videos.  You really have to get past your plastic looking people in the animations and just enjoy the missions themselves.  Thankfully the videos and the gameplay are completely and totally different.

title: beatbuddy: tale of the guardians
text: The game had potential as a music puzzle type but it just fell flat. The game has good visuals with almost no glitches and has good game mechanics (with a mouse anyways). There are two different modes: 1 with a vehicle and one with you moving around which offers a good change of pace once in a while so you don't get bored. However, the puzzles are simply get the key to the door with increasingly complicated ways and are not that challenging. The soundtrack had its moments but the same 10 second loop gets ANNOYING after a while. There is a story there with something about taking over the music or something but its so underdevoloped that you basically can skip all of it. Also, its very short (I took my time and beat it in 6 hours). There are collectibles but I just basically gave that up realizing that all it had were extras. Overall, it had potential but it lacked a good amount of challange. As a simple way to pass the time, not bad but you can do better.

text: PLEASE READ WARNING AT THE END. Here are the basic details from my experiences in the game: -There are levels, albeit not many and it's been over a year since I have bought the game and I have noticed that they have introduced a new sandbox and the empty sandbox among various bugfixes, but no new levels, so dont go in expecting a fully fledged "campaign" so all in all you get a small campagin that may take you an hour or two, maybe even less to complete and you get 3 sandboxes to mess around in, the old sandbox, new sandbox and the barren expanse (empty sandbox). -You build siege machines, planes, airships, tanks, etc. If you have an idea for a killing machine, then you can most probably build it in Beseige. -Workshop content is a lot of fun to play with, especially hillclimbers and off road vehicles. -The building system can be quite a learning curve, especially when you try and build a flying machine. -Graphics are nice to look at, no complaints. -Game is quite cheap and you can squeeze quite a few hours out of it. Overall, for $9.99 I cant really complain. If you enjoy games that allow you to create various machines/vehicles, buy Besiege. It's a small game with not a lot of content as of yet but to be honest building is where you will spend most of your time. WARNING: Unless you have a ♥♥♥♥ing beast of a PC, I do not recommend you buy this game. I originally had this game on my laptop, it ran, but when creating medium sized machines the FPS would hit around 15-20. I built a gaming rig 2 months back, its pretty high end to be honest yet when I try to build a big machine or try to load a player created machine that has a decent amount of parts, the game goes down to like 10 FPS, coompletley unplayable and it takes away from the creation factor. I want to build and play big machines but I cannot because for some reason my high end PC cannot handle it, maybe the game is just terribly optimized, I can run all new games flawlessly bar this one. I know the game is in early access, but come on, its been over a year since its initial release. If not for the low FPS issue I would give this game a 9/10, I enjoy it, but this one issue ruins it for me so I cant help but give this game 6/10 (in its current state).

title: besiege
text: Besiege is a great game, the campaign is pretty challenging. While, the developers intended for people to send most of thier time in the campaign, I have noticed that most people spend most of their time in the freebuild mode. The campaign is great and all but, the programmers should definitly focus on the freebuild aswell. The first problem I have withh besiege is that there are not enough different parts to build a machiene with, at first this might not seem like a problem at first, but after playing for a while you think to yourself that "I can build this, this, and that... if I had this, this and that." while that is the only major gripe I have with the game. One of my favorite features of Besiege is that you can go back to any beaten campaign level and freebuild in it. But the best part of Besiege is the small quaint community behind it, people are always sharing new creations, and skin pack on the Steam Workshop. Pros: -The community -The ability to use campaign levels as free build maps -All the crazy creations on the Steam Workshop - Another nod to the great community -The campaign to an extent -map creation Cons -lack of of parts While, the game might look shallow and boring on the outside. But, Besiege is a thought provoking game with an original concept I haven't seen done better. Overall I would strongly recommend this game
